findings.title: idx_t mapped to signed intp instead of uint64 in several count/size/index signatures (inconsistent with duckdb.h and with sibling entries)
findings.description: duckdb.h defines idx_t as uint64_t, and CLAUDE.md states the mapping convention 'idx_t -> uint64_t -> uint64'. Most entries follow it: duckdb_nparams (:217), duckdb_get_list_size (:189), duckdb_rows_changed (:227), duckdb_struct_type_child_count (:228), duckdb_union_type_member_count (:231), duckdb_array_type_array_size (:78) all return uint64 for an idx_t; and idx_t index args in duckdb_get_list_child/_map_key/_struct_child (:188,190,193) are uint64. But five entries map the same idx_t to signed intp: return values of duckdb_column_count (:106), duckdb_row_count (:226), duckdb_data_chunk_get_column_count (:156), duckdb_data_chunk_get_size (:157) are all idx_t (uint64_t) in the C API yet declared intp; and the idx_t argument of duckdb_data_chunk_get_vector (2nd arg, :158) and duckdb_validity_row_is_valid (2nd arg 'row', :234) are declared intp instead of uint64. Because intp is signed int64 and idx_t is uint64, and both are 64-bit INTEGER-class in the ABI, the register lowering is byte-identical, so there is NO runtime miscomputation for any realistic count/row value (< 2^63). The defect is purely type fidelity: it deviates from duckdb.h and from the module's own convention, and produces avoidable numba int/uint signature friction (a uint64 result from one binding fed into an intp-typed argument of another, or vice versa, forces an implicit signed/unsigned cast).
findings.impact: No runtime corruption on any supported platform (ABI-identical 64-bit integer passing). Cosmetic/convention deviation only; minor numba signed/unsigned interop friction and reduced fidelity to duckdb.h.
findings.recommendation: For strict fidelity, change these five entries to use uint64 for the idx_t return/arg positions: duckdb_column_count -> uint64(intp); duckdb_row_count -> uint64(intp); duckdb_data_chunk_get_column_count -> uint64(intp); duckdb_data_chunk_get_size -> uint64(intp); duckdb_data_chunk_get_vector -> intp(intp, uint64); duckdb_validity_row_is_valid -> int8(intp, uint64). This aligns them with the idx_t entries already using uint64 elsewhere in the file. Low priority given zero runtime impact.

findings.title: duckdb_vector_get_validity return typed uint64 but the C return is a pointer (uint64_t *) — violates the 'all pointers are intp' invariant
findings.description: duckdb.h declares 'uint64_t *duckdb_vector_get_validity(duckdb_vector vector);' — the return value is a POINTER to the validity bitmask (or NULL). The signature declares the return as uint64 (an unsigned integer value), not intp. Every other pointer-returning binding in the file uses intp (e.g. duckdb_vector_get_data :236 -> intp, duckdb_data_chunk_get_vector :158 -> intp, all duckdb_value/logical_type/char* returns -> intp), and the module invariant (understanding note, invariant #2) is 'every pointer is intp (signed 64-bit)'. Returning uint64 for a pointer is byte-identical at the ABI level (the address is delivered in RAX either way, and canonical user-space addresses < 2^48 are non-negative in both int64 and uint64), so there is no runtime dereference error. However, the returned uint64 is normally passed straight into duckdb_validity_row_is_valid(validity_p, row), whose 1st arg is intp (:234), so this binding hands a uint64 into an intp-typed pointer parameter, forcing an implicit unsigned->signed cast and breaking the otherwise-uniform intp pointer typing.
findings.impact: No runtime corruption (address bits are identical; validity pointers are well below 2^63). Type-fidelity/consistency deviation: a pointer typed as a non-pointer unsigned integer, causing numba signed/unsigned friction at the consuming call site.
findings.recommendation: Change the signature at :237 to intp(intp) to match every other pointer-returning binding and the module's pointer convention: signatures['duckdb_vector_get_validity'] = intp(intp). Low priority given zero runtime impact.

notes: Audited all enum values (duckdb.h duckdb_type, :23-66), the type aliases (:17-75), and every signatures[...] entry (:78-274) against the DuckDB C API for the 1.3.2-1.5.x range. No local duckdb.h was available; verification is against knowledge of the DuckDB C API plus the project's documented conventions and the numbox ABI contract (numbox/core/bindings/call.py). Overall the signatures are sound; only two low-severity type-fidelity inconsistencies were found (both ABI-identical, zero runtime miscomputation). Items explicitly checked and judged CORRECT: (1) all struct-shaped aliases match the C layouts byte-for-byte -- duckdb_result_ty UniTuple(intp,6)=48B, hugeint Tuple((uint64,int64)), uhugeint UniTuple(uint64,2), interval Tuple((int32,int32,int64))=16B non-canonical INT/INT (correctly relies on numbox's _needs_int_int_eightbyte_repack), decimal Tuple((uint8,uint8,uint64,int64))=24B with the nested hugeint at offset 8, blob/bit Tuple((intp,uint64))=16B, varint Tuple((intp,uint64,int8))=24B. (2) duckdb_state_ty=int32 with DuckDBSuccess=0/DuckDBError=1 matches the C enum. (3) duckdb_type enum values 0-38 match duckdb.h exactly, including the out-of-order UHUGEINT=32/ARRAY=33/ANY=34; TIME_NS=39 is plausible for 1.4+/1.5+ (value not independently confirmable without the header, but it is an unused constant with no signature dependency). (4) VARINT=35 / BIGNUM=35 dual-alias and the proxy_if_available gating of duckdb_create_varint/duckdb_get_varint are internally consistent; even if 'BIGNUM' is a fictional or renamed constant, it is unused in any signature, so it cannot cause a binding-level defect. (5) struct-by-value vs pointer choices are correct: single-field structs passed as their scalar (duckdb_date->int32, duckdb_time/timestamp->int64, duckdb_time_tz->uint64), 16B by-value in/out (hugeint/uhugeint/uuid/interval/bit/blob), 24B LARGE in/out (decimal/varint). (6) _p/_pp usage and out-pointer args (duckdb_open/connect/prepare/query/bind_parameter_index) all correctly use intp. The three _call_lib_func_byval entries (duckdb_fetch_chunk :172/946, duckdb_result_return_type :224/1132, duckdb_result_statement_type :225/1138) declare duckdb_result_ty=UniTuple(intp,6)=48B and are exercised on Linux x86-64 CI; the declared arg type is documentation-only for the byval path (numbox lowers from the caller's actual value type), and the code is tested/merged, so no defect is asserted there.
